OpenCode Go Limits and Usage Calculator

OpenCode Go pools paid model usage across one allowance. The 5-hour window allows 20% of the monthly allowance and the week allows 50%. Check the Go page in OpenCode Console for the window you hit. Switching models does not reset the limit, and Extra Usage can draw on your credits.

What does your Go usage meter show?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Check which Go limit you hit

  1. Open your workspace in OpenCode Console and open Go. For Teams, check the member whose API key made the requests.
  2. Compare the three usage readings. A full 5-hour window becomes available when the five hours end. The weekly window resets Monday at 00:00 UTC. Monthly usage resets when your next paid period begins.
  3. Check every window before retrying. If two windows are full, the earlier reset alone may leave you blocked. If none is full, verify the selected provider and chosen model before treating the error as a quota issue.

If you want to avoid using credits after the included allowance runs out, check that Extra Usage is off before sending more requests. The Go docs say Teams starts with it on. To keep working without using Extra Usage credits, select an available free model or wait for the limiting windows to reset.

No full window or unclear error?

Confirm the provider shows OpenCode Go and compare the selected model with the current Go model list. Use the Console for the same workspace and, on Teams, the same member. If the model is unavailable despite remaining allowance, check its access requirements and the exact provider error before retrying.

Calculate how much of a window you used

Enter the usage cost of each paid model in one window and its monthly limit for your plan. Find monthly limits in the current Go model table. These limits are model-specific usage values, separate from the subscription price. For usage that spans prices or plans, use the Console meter.

Model 1
Model 2 (optional)

For a single model, leave both fields in the second row blank. This calculator runs in your browser and does not read your account. To compare windows, calculate each separately using that window’s own usage.

Worked example for two models

Suppose you used $2 on a model with a $20 monthly limit and $3 on one with a $60 limit, both in the same five hours. Divide each usage cost by its own limit: 2 ÷ 20 = 10%, and 3 ÷ 60 = 5%. Together that’s 15% of the monthly allowance. Divide 15% by the 5-hour cap of 20%: you used 75% of that 5-hour window. Those values are hypothetical; your Console shows what actually counted.

For a weekly calculation divide the summed monthly share by 50%; for a paid month divide by 100%. Reaching 100% of a window means you reached that cap in the example. It does not tell you when it resets or how many requests fit.

Use the limits for your Go plan

Go is $10 per month, Go Plus is $40 per month, and Go Teams is $20 per member per month with a two-member minimum. Teams members have separate allowances, each shared across their own paid models. Use the model limit for the member and plan you’re checking.

Source: OpenCode’s Go limits and model rules, checked Nov 24, 2026. The provider’s per-request allowance and Console readings are the reference for actual usage.
